..$comment-ported: Ported from forge-play/Forge, the fleet standard. Keep the shape identical unless this repo has a reason of its own — divergent copies of a release pipeline are how one repo silently stops publishing.
..$comment-versioning: release-type 'simple' maintains CHANGELOG.md and the tag and edits no version file — correct here because hatch-vcs derives the version from the tag, so there is no second copy to keep in step. bump-minor-pre-major FALSE with bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major false means, below 1.0: feat -> minor, fix and everything unlabelled -> patch, a breaking change -> 1.0.0. CORRECTED 2026-09-11, the hard way: a 0.0.0 manifest does NOT make the first release 0.1.0. With no prior release, release-please's FIRST release is 1.0.0 whatever the manifest says — it cut and published exactly that before this claim was tested. Use `initial-version` here before a first release, or a `Release-As: <version>` commit footer to force one. Every release AFTER the first bumps from the manifest as described. WHAT IS NOT GUARANTEED: this keys off the commit type, so it only holds when a breaking change is written `feat!:` or carries a BREAKING CHANGE footer. A break mislabelled `refactor:` still ships as a patch.
..$comment-what-cuts-a-release: EVERY type above without "hidden": true cuts a release on its own — not just feat and fix. In the fleet a single ci: commit once tagged and published a version containing nothing a user installs. release-please.yml arms auto-merge, so an un-hidden type ships to PyPI unattended, and a PyPI version can never be reused.
..$comment-hidden-rule: The line is: does this commit change what someone gets from `pip install willow-corpus-lens`? docs/test/ci do not — tests and workflows are not packaged, and a README edit only moves the PyPI page — so they are hidden and ride along with the next real release. build and deps stay visible because a packaging change genuinely alters the installed artifact. refactor and perf stay visible because they change shipped code. Hidden also means absent from CHANGELOG.md: release-please has no 'list it but do not release on it' setting, so this is a real trade, taken deliberately.
..$comment-wall: A release is also a wall event: the published artifact is the thing strangers run on their own logs. A commit that changes what leaves the wall (guard.py, the audit sentence, an adapter's quarantine handling) is never `chore:` or `refactor:` — it is `feat:`, `fix:` or `security:`, so it gets a version number someone can point at.
..$comment-first-release-changelog: tools/changelog_dedup.py cannot correct a FIRST release's section: its matcher expects the `## [x.y.z](…/compare/…)` heading release-please writes for every release after the first, and a first release has no previous tag to compare against. The 1.0.0 section shipped with every entry duplicated (the real commit and the merge commit carrying its title). Fix the tool in forge-play first, then re-sync, per its docstring.
